title: Roman Egypt: prices of wheat and barley, AD 3-350, in drachmas per artaba, one row per document (Kelly 2021, Appendix 2)
source: P. V. Kelly, 'Third-Century Price Inflation Reassessed', Theoretical Roman Archaeology Journal 4(1): 5 (2021), doi:10.16995/traj.4338; Supplementary file 2, 'Appendix 2, database of prices', doi:10.16995/traj.4338.s2 (traj-4338-kelly.docx)
series: table (wheat_private, wheat_state, barley: tables 'Private Wheat Prices pre-AD 274', 'State Wheat Prices pre-AD 274', 'Barley Prices pre-AD 274'; wheat_post274, barley_post274: 'Wheat prices post-AD 274', 'Barley Prices post-AD 274'); date (as printed in the appendix, AD); year_from, year_to (the range the date names; empty where it cannot be read as a year or range); year (midpoint of the range); uncertain (1 where the date carries '?' or 'c.' or cannot be read); amounts (the appendix's column of prices, verbatim); dr_per_artaba (median of the readable prices of the document, in drachmas per artaba; obols at 6 to the drachma before AD 190 and 7 after, talents at 6,000 drachmas); n_prices (number of prices behind the median); nature, nome, reference (verbatim from the appendix)

citation: Source: P. V. Kelly (2021), 'Third-Century Price Inflation Reassessed', Theoretical Roman Archaeology Journal 4(1): 5, doi:10.16995/traj.4338, Appendix 2 (doi:10.16995/traj.4338.s2), CC BY 4.0; medians per document computed by data/fetch/kelly_prices.py.
notes: 130 rows: 40 private wheat prices and 31 state wheat prices before AD 274 (Kelly's counts, 2021 p. 14), 25 barley prices before 274, 23 wheat prices and 11 barley prices after 274. Kelly compiled the prices from the documentary papyri (Duke Databank of Documentary Papyri, checked against earlier collections; his Appendix 1 gives the details). Following Kelly (2021, pp. 6 and 8), a document with several prices is reduced to their median and a range of dates is placed at its midpoint; obols are converted at 6 to the drachma before AD 190 and 7 after (Kelly p. 8, citing Rathbone 1997). A price marked '<' (an upper bound) is left out of the median, '10+' is read as 10, and where the appendix gives two readings and says 'Assumed to be' one of them, that one is used; '13 and 1/3rd talents' is one price, '54[0]' (a digit restored by the editor of the papyrus) is 540, and in a list that mentions talents a bare number below 1,000 is in talents and a larger one in drachmas (true of every such list in the appendix). Kelly's text (p. 8) says that the thirteen prices of P.Mich. II 123 for AD 45 are treated as one point with a median of 3.0 drachmas; in the appendix, the AD 45 row is P.Mich. II 127 (six prices, median 7.445) and P.Mich. II 123 appears under AD 46 with one price of 8.73. The snapshot follows the appendix and the chapter says so.
